nodes.description: Token name string derived from the staking token name, set in initialize().
Token symbol string derived from the staking token symbol, set in initialize().
Token decimals copied from the staking token in initialize().
Constant 7 days used to floor timestamps to weekly epochs.
Constant maximum lock duration (4 * 365 * 86400) used to bound lockup end and compute slope.
mapping(address => Checkpoint[]) holding per-user voting power checkpoints.
mapping(address => uint256) index of the latest user checkpoint, used as epoch counter and max epoch.
Checkpoint[] holding the aggregated global voting power history.
Index of the latest global checkpoint; incremented as new global checkpoints are pushed.
mapping(address => Lockup) storing each user's locked amount and lock end time.
mapping(uint256 => int128) of scheduled slope changes at weekly timestamps.
ERC20 token contract that users lock and that is transferred in lockup()/withdraw().
Public function that creates or extends a token lockup, transfers the staking token delta and writes checkpoints.
Public function that withdraws all staking tokens from an expired lockup and clears the lockup record.
External function that forces a global checkpoint to be written.
Private function writing user checkpoints, updating userEpoch and adjusting slopeChanges for old/new lockups.
Private function iterating weekly epochs to fill global checkpoints and update globalEpoch.
Initializer setting staking token, metadata and pushing the first global checkpoint.
View function returning current user voting power by decaying the last checkpoint bias with block.timestamp.
View function returning a user's historical voting power at a given block using binary search over checkpoints.
View function returning historical total voting supply at a given block number.
Internal view function iterating weekly slope changes to compute total supply at a given time.
Internal binary search returning the most recent checkpoint epoch before a given block.
UUPS upgrade authorization restricted to the contract owner.
Delegatee assignment stub that always reverts, meaning no delegation support exists.
View function returning the global voting supply at the current block timestamp.
Caller-controlled address that selects lockups, receives withdrawals and gates owner-only functions.
Miner-influenceable timestamp used for lockup validation, decay math and epoch iteration.
External ERC20 safeTransferFrom call in lockup() that pulls the deposit delta from the user.
External ERC20 safeTransfer call in withdraw() that pushes the locked amount back to the user.
User-supplied amount of staking tokens to lock in lockup().
User-supplied lockup end timestamp in lockup(), floored to a weekly boundary.
Local difference between the new and old locked amount, used as the transferred value.
Local copy of the caller's previous lockup used to compute checkpoint deltas and events.
Local struct of the new lockup amount/end written to storage and to checkpoints.

edges.reason: msg.sender selects which lockup entry is read/written and is the payer of the staking token transfer in lockup().
msg.sender determines which lockup is cleared and is the recipient of the token transfer in withdraw().
_authorizeUpgrade is guarded by onlyOwner, which compares owner() to msg.sender.
delegate() is callable by any msg.sender but unconditionally reverts, so no delegation can be granted.
block.timestamp is relied upon to validate the new lockup end, the extension ordering and MAX_LOCK_TIME bounds.
block.timestamp determines whether the lockup is expired and the withdrawal is permitted.
block.timestamp drives the bias/slope computation and scheduled slope changes for user checkpoints.
block.timestamp terminates the weekly iteration loop that writes global checkpoints.
balanceOf decays the last checkpoint bias using block.timestamp minus the checkpoint timestamp.
_supplyAt applies slope changes relative to the supplied time parameter derived from block timestamps.
lockup() executes an external ERC20 safeTransferFrom to the staking token contract.
withdraw() executes an external ERC20 safeTransfer to msg.sender via SafeERC20.
withdraw() transfers tokens to msg.sender before _writeUserCheckpoint finalizes the user voting state.
lockup() calls _writeUserCheckpoint after the external transfer to record the new voting position.
lockup() invokes _writeUserCheckpoint with the old and new lockup structures.
withdraw() invokes _writeUserCheckpoint with the old lockup and a zeroed lockup.
_writeUserCheckpoint calls _writeGlobalCheckpoint passing user slope and bias deltas.
checkpoint() calls _writeGlobalCheckpoint with zero deltas to refresh global state.
_writeGlobalCheckpoint pushes new Checkpoint entries into _globalCheckpoints.
_writeUserCheckpoint pushes old and new Checkpoint entries into _userCheckpoints.
_writeUserCheckpoint reads and updates scheduled slope changes in slopeChanges.
_writeGlobalCheckpoint reads slopeChanges for each weekly iteration step.
_writeUserCheckpoint increments and stores the user epoch in userEpoch.
_writeGlobalCheckpoint increments globalEpoch for every checkpoint appended.
balanceOf reads userEpoch to locate the latest user checkpoint.
balanceOf reads the latest checkpoint from _userCheckpoints.
balanceOfAt uses the _findEpoch binary search over user and global checkpoints.
balanceOfAt reads global checkpoints to estimate the block timestamp of the queried block.
totalSupplyAt uses _findEpoch to locate the global checkpoint for the queried block.
totalSupplyAt calls _supplyAt to compute the supply at the estimated time.
_supplyAt reads slopeChanges to decay bias across weekly intervals.
lockup() enforces the MAX_LOCK_TIME ceiling on the requested end timestamp.
_writeUserCheckpoint divides locked amount by MAX_LOCK_TIME to derive the voting slope.
lockup() reads and overwrites the caller's Lockup record in the lockups mapping.
withdraw() reads and zeroes the caller's Lockup record in the lockups mapping.
totalSupply reads the latest global checkpoint from _globalCheckpoints.
totalSupply delegates supply computation to _supplyAt at block.timestamp.
The _amount parameter flows into the cast, validation and delta computation of lockup().
The _end parameter is floored to a week, validated and stored as the new lockup end.
The amountDelta local is the exact value passed to the external safeTransferFrom call.
The oldLockup local provides the old slope/bias and old end needed for checkpoint deltas.
The newLockup local provides the new slope/bias and new end needed for checkpoint deltas.
_writeUserCheckpoint performs int128 slope/bias arithmetic over timestamp differences, which can truncate or overflow.

normalization_plan.reason: User-supplied function parameter of lockup(); it has no independent security identity and is fully absorbed by the lockup() node that validates and stores it.
User-supplied end timestamp parameter of lockup(); it is floored, validated against block.timestamp/MAX_LOCK_TIME and stored, so it merges into lockup().
Local variable computed only to be passed as the value argument of the external safeTransferFrom call, so it folds into that unsafe_operation node.
Local copy of the caller's previous lockup used solely within lockup()/withdraw() checkpoint logic, so it merges into the lockup() node.
Local struct of the new lockup assembled and persisted inside lockup(); it carries no separate security meaning beyond the lockup() node.
